themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Surge This Week
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints in Central Harlem spiked to 5 reports this week, a 400% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 1.0 complaint per week, representing the most acute safety concern emerging in the district right now.
evidence: 5 drug activity complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.62)
400% spike represents statistically significant deviation from baseline patterns
Timing coincides with warm weather period when street activity typically increases
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD precinct commander about drug enforcement strategy and resources in Central Harlem; cross-reference with recent seizure or arrest data
Speak with residents and local business owners about which blocks are most affected and what specific drug activity they're observing (dealing, consumption, etc.)

themes_detail.label: Residential Waste Disposal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints nearly quadrupled to 9 reports this week, a 279% spike above the 8-week average of 2.4 weekly complaints, signaling an emerging sanitation management problem across the district.
evidence: 9 residential disposal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.43)
279% increase suggests new or worsening waste management issue, not seasonal fluctuation
Aligns with broader sanitation concerns: 1,246 unsanitary condition complaints and 513 dirty condition complaints over 90 days
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Sanitation to determine if there are collection route changes, staffing shortages, or equipment breakdowns affecting the district
Visit specific blocks with high complaint density to document waste accumulation and interview residents about collection frequency

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints surged to 4 reports this week, a 300% increase from the 8-week baseline of 1.0 complaint per week, indicating accelerated environmental degradation in parks and streetscapes.
evidence: 4 illegal tree damage complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.24)
300% spike suggests concentrated, recent damage—potentially from construction, vandalism, or storm-related activity
Converges with park noise spike (8 complaints 2 weeks ago, 700% above baseline), suggesting heightened activity in district green spaces
reporting_angles: Visit Central Harlem parks (Marcus Garvey, St. Nicholas Terrace area, etc.) to document tree damage, identify common locations, and photograph for visual storytelling
Interview NYC Parks department on whether illegal construction work or arborist violations are being investigated

themes_detail.label: Park Noise and Nuisance Clustering
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints peaked at 8 reports two weeks ago—a 700% spike above the 8-week average of 1.0 complaint per week—suggesting concentrated outdoor disturbances, potentially from unregulated events or gathering patterns.
evidence: 8 park noise complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.26)
700% spike concentrated in warm-weather window, suggesting seasonal events or organized gatherings
Converges with illegal tree damage spike this week and drinking complaints spike 2 weeks ago, all pointing to elevated park activity and possible management gaps
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks and NYPD for incident reports and details on which parks generated complaints; determine if specific events (music events, street vending clusters, etc.) are involved
Attend district parks during peak hours to observe patterns and document noise sources; interview residents about frequency and timing

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk and Pedestrian Environment Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints hit 15 reports two weeks ago, a 200% increase above the 8-week average of 5.0 weekly complaints, pointing to accumulated pedestrian infrastructure decay affecting walkability across the district.
evidence: 15 sidewalk condition complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 5.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.77)
200% spike reflects recent deterioration—potentially from weather damage, lack of maintenance, or concentrated cracking in specific corridors
Aligns with long-standing community board request for infrastructure upgrades and 470 active DOB alteration filings suggesting construction activity may be disrupting street conditions
reporting_angles: Document specific blocks with worst sidewalk conditions via photos and GPS mapping; cross-reference with 311 complaints to identify hotspots
Interview NYC Department of Transportation about maintenance schedules and capital repair timelines for Central Harlem; ask about backlog
